items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: He was a virtuoso according to George Fields and my grandfather and Manny Perez.

ctx.x: How did you get started on your first instrument?

First instrument, there had a lot of drums around the house. I had three uncles who played drums. Paul Bowman, Lloyd Bowman, and Lucien Bowman. They all played drums. So naturally I'd sit behind Lucien's drums. He'd always play with those 56th Ray Jazz bands, and they'd be mad at us. So I'd sit around and have intermissions, or if there was a low, I'd play the drums. So I'm going to keep the beat. Of course I got the beat. And then it was suggested I learned to play kindly, because we had a great clan that played…

items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1976-02-04
items.q: he heard the best he knew, Papa C, he heard everybody here and at that time they were great trumpet players and he, I was all about there, he, he came out of that which is nitty-gritty black American earth lifestyle. ... Manny Perez had two, first and second trumpet.

ctx.x: what was the difference in their style?

Well, there's a big difference. one was lyrical which from, from a classical vein, technically musical because Bix was a, uh, was interested in concert music and Debussy and Ravel and his thing was semi-classical, that In the Mist and a couple of piano pieces he wrote which had a, a great significance of creative inventiveness but based from a European, a classical vein where Louis stuff was so black out of the Baptist Church and out of the honky tonks and, uh, out of, uh, a tradition of New Orleans trumpet…

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Then there was Manny Perez. ... Seen him do that with Manny Perez’s band.

ctx.x: Yeah. Manny Perez or [Vic] Gaspard, trombone. [Tom “Oke”] Gaspard’s brother.

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: And there was a rivalry between Manny Perez and George Moret... And I'm hearing this. And my uncles, they're talkin' about who's who and who ain't.

ctx.x: Well, I didn't think about it too much. I was going to school. And I'm hearing this music all the time, and I'd see these musicians, they're celebrated. I've got four uncles -- Paul Barbarin, Louis Barbarin, Lucien Barbarin, Willie Barbarin. We live in the neighborhood, in the Seventh Ward, where there's quite a few halls -- the (?) Hall, the Jean Ami Hall, the Franz(?) Ami Hall, the New Hall. And on Ledgerfield Avenue there was about four or five White halls. And there was music all the time. And I'm listening…

And my uncles... My grandfather being in the brass band, he played the funerals with the Onward Brass Band, which was the greatest brass band at that time. And there was a rivalry between Manny Perez and George Moret(?), who was the leader of the Excelsior Band. And I'm hearing this. And my uncles, they're talkin' about who's who and who ain't. And it's a celebrate thing, and everybody is celebrated. So they would talk who could play and who couldn't, and who rated... Like most people, the kids in town, they…
